skill.name: container-hadolint
skill.description: Guides Dockerfile linting with Hadolint, explains security findings, and supplies reusable configurations for local and CI workflows.
skill.summary: Review Dockerfiles with Hadolint guidance, remediation examples, and CI templates.
skill.author: AgentSecOps

security_audit.summary: Most alerts are false positives from Markdown, reference links, placeholder credentials, and examples labeled as insecure. Actionable risks include unsafe CI filename handling and unverified latest-binary downloads. Mutable CI dependencies add supply-chain exposure, while no prompt injection or malicious intent was found.

remediation.issue: Repository filenames can influence CI shell parsing
remediation.suggestion: Use null-delimited file discovery and loops, then pass values through environment variables without direct expression interpolation.

remediation.issue: Hadolint binaries are downloaded from a mutable latest URL
remediation.suggestion: Pin an exact Hadolint release and verify its published checksum before making the binary executable.

remediation.issue: CI actions and images use mutable version references
remediation.suggestion: Pin GitHub Actions to commit hashes and GitLab container images to immutable digests, then review updates through automation.

content.value_statement: Dockerfile mistakes can create insecure and unreliable container images. This skill provides Hadolint workflows, rule guidance, remediation examples, and reusable CI configurations.
actual_capabilities: Explains Hadolint installation and local Dockerfile scanning with native binaries or Docker.
Provides strict, balanced, and permissive Hadolint configuration templates.
Provides GitHub Actions and GitLab CI templates for automated Dockerfile checks.
Shows report generation for JSON, SARIF, GitLab Code Quality, and Checkstyle consumers.
Explains selected Hadolint findings with insecure and improved Dockerfile examples.
limitations: Requires Hadolint or Docker; the skill does not include an executable scanner.
Analyzes Dockerfile source and does not scan built images, running containers, or package vulnerabilities.
Bundled references cover selected rules and should not replace current Hadolint or CIS documentation.
CI templates need dependency pinning, integrity checks, and safer handling of repository filenames.

use_cases.title: Review a Dockerfile
use_cases.description: Identify lint findings, understand their impact, and receive focused remediation steps before building an image.

use_cases.title: Standardize CI checks
use_cases.description: Adapt the supplied workflow and configuration templates to enforce shared Dockerfile policies.

use_cases.title: Assess container controls
use_cases.description: Compare Dockerfile practices with selected security guidance and document prioritized remediation.

prompt_templates.title: Lint one Dockerfile
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [Dockerfile path] with Hadolint. Explain each finding in plain language and suggest the smallest secure change.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a policy
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare the strict, balanced, and permissive configurations for [project context]. Recommend one and explain every necessary customization.
prompt_templates.scenario: Select a configuration for a team

prompt_templates.title: Build a CI gate
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Hadolint check for [GitHub Actions or GitLab CI]. Pin dependencies, handle all filenames safely, and define failure thresholds.

prompt_templates.title: Plan advanced remediation
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze Hadolint results for [repository]. Group root causes, prioritize security impact, identify justified suppressions, and propose a phased remediation plan.

output_examples.input: Review a Dockerfile that uses a mutable base image tag and runs as root.
output: High priority: add a non-root runtime user and switch before the final command.
Reproducibility: replace the mutable base tag with an approved version or digest.
Validation: rerun Hadolint and document any remaining suppression.

output_examples.input: Recommend a CI policy for a legacy repository with several Dockerfiles.
output_examples.output: Start with the balanced policy, report warnings without blocking, then raise thresholds after the baseline findings are assigned and remediated.

output_examples.input: Explain a warning about unpinned operating system packages.
output_examples.output: Unpinned packages reduce reproducibility and can introduce unexpected updates. Pin supported versions and keep update, installation, and cache cleanup in one layer.

best_practices: Use the balanced configuration as a baseline, then document every override and ignored rule.
Pin CI actions, container images, and downloaded binaries to immutable versions with integrity verification.
Combine Hadolint with image, vulnerability, and secret scanning for broader container assurance.
anti_patterns: Do not treat a clean Hadolint result as proof that a container image is secure.
Do not copy mutable download or CI examples into production without pinning and verification.
Do not suppress findings globally before confirming their context and security impact.

faq.question: What does this skill analyze?
faq.answer: It guides Hadolint analysis of Dockerfile instructions, configuration choices, findings, and remediation.

faq.question: Does it install or run Hadolint automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides commands and templates, while the user or agent runs Hadolint in the selected environment.

faq.question: Can it scan container images?
faq.answer: No. Use an image scanner for operating system packages, application dependencies, malware, and runtime configuration.

faq.question: Which CI systems are covered?
faq.answer: The bundled templates cover GitHub Actions and GitLab CI.

faq.question: Does a clean result prove CIS compliance?
faq.answer: No. Hadolint findings support selected practices, but formal compliance requires current control mapping, evidence, and broader validation.

faq.question: How should false positives be handled?
faq.answer: Review the context, document the justification, and use narrow rule overrides instead of broad global suppressions.
